Todd's mention of Disco Demolition reminded me of another pivotal moment in music history: The death of Andy Wood. (I cannot recommend the article in the link enough for alt-rock fans, by the way.)
 Wood's death came right before the Seattle sound hit it big, and the fingerprints of that event were all over that Nirvana-led first wave: It inspired both Alice in Chains' signature song, "Would," and the cinematic grunge showcase, Singles, the film Cameron Crowe made between Say Anything... and Jerry Macguire. Wood's roommate, Soundgarden frontman Chris Cornell, gave Eddie Vedder his first on-album appearance and early grunge a bonus album with the self-titled Temple of the Dog.
